title: Money Moves From Tech to Safer Stocks
body: On Tuesday, U.S. investors **rotated** out of big tech stocks and into older, steadier (더 안정적인) companies. The S&P 500 rose 0.22% to 7,707.57, and the Dow jumped 0.95%, or about 492 points. The Nasdaq, full of tech names, ended almost flat at -0.02%. Health care was the star. A popular health care **sector** fund climbed about 2.2% during the day and hit a **record high**. Investors like these **defensive** stocks because people need medicine even in bad times. General Motors fell about 7.5%. Its profit beat forecasts (예상치), but its full-year **guidance** of $12.75 to $13.75 per share was lower than analysts (애널리스트) expected. In Korea, the picture was darker. On the same day, the KOSPI dropped 3.7% to 5,552.74, and foreign investors sold about 0.5 trillion won of stocks. Over 20 trading days, the KOSPI has lost 17.3%, while the S&P 500 has lost only 1.0%. The lesson: two markets can move very differently, even in the same week.
ko: 화요일 미국 투자자들은 대형 기술주에서 빠져나와 더 오래되고 안정적인 기업들로 돈을 옮겼다(로테이션). S&P500은 0.22% 오른 7,707.57에 마감했고, 다우는 0.95%, 약 492포인트 뛰었다. 기술주가 많은 나스닥은 -0.02%로 거의 제자리였다. 주인공은 헬스케어였다. 대표 헬스케어 섹터 펀드(ETF)는 장중 약 2.2% 올라 사상 최고치를 찍었다. 사람들은 경기가 나빠도 약은 필요하기 때문에 투자자들은 이런 방어주를 좋아한다. 반면 GM(제너럴모터스)은 약 7.5% 떨어졌다. 분기 이익은 예상을 넘었지만, 주당 12.75~13.75달러라는 연간 가이던스(회사 전망치)가 애널리스트 기대보다 낮았다. 한국은 분위기가 더 어두웠다. 같은 날 코스피는 3.7% 하락한 5,552.74로 마감했고, 외국인은 약 0.5조 원어치 주식을 팔았다. 최근 20거래일 동안 코스피는 17.3% 빠졌지만 S&P500은 1.0%만 빠졌다. 교훈: 같은 주에도 두 시장은 전혀 다르게 움직일 수 있다.

vocab.en_easy: To move money from one group of stocks to another group.
vocab.ex: Investors rotated from tech stocks into health care stocks.

vocab.en_easy: A group of companies that do the same kind of business.
vocab.ex: The energy sector did well when oil prices went up.
The health care fund hit a record high on Tuesday.

vocab.en_easy: Not hurt much when the economy is bad.
vocab.ex: When the market is scary, some people buy defensive stocks like food and medicine companies.

vocab.en_easy: A company's own guess about its future sales or profit.
vocab.ex: The stock fell because the company's guidance was weak.

grammar.quote: into older, steadier companies / In Korea, the picture was darker.
grammar.explain_ko: 짧은 형용사는 -er(old→older, dark→darker), y로 끝나면 y→ier(steady→steadier). 긴 형용사는 more를 붙인다(more stable). OPIc 비교 문제에서 필수.
examples: My gym is bigger than my old one.
Coffee is more expensive these days than it was five years ago.

grammar.quote: the KOSPI has lost 17.3%, while the S&P 500 has lost only 1.0%.
grammar.explain_ko: 두 사실을 나란히 놓고 차이를 보여줄 때 while을 쓴다. '과거 vs 현재' 비교 답변에 그대로 쓸 수 있다.
examples: Back then I only did cardio, while now I mostly lift weights.
Tech stocks fell, while health care stocks went up.

tense.why_ko: 어제(화요일) 끝난 하루의 결과라서 단순 과거. 뉴스의 '어제 종가'는 거의 항상 과거형.

tense.sentence: Over 20 trading days, the KOSPI has lost 17.3%.
tense.why_ko: 20일 전부터 지금까지 이어진 변화의 '누적 결과'라서 has lost. 'over + 기간'과 잘 어울린다.

review.q: 'Market breadth is weak' 에서 breadth의 뜻은?
choices: 상승 종목의 폭(얼마나 많은 종목이 함께 오르는지)
review.exp_ko: breadth = 폭. 지수만 오르는지, 많은 종목이 함께 오르는지를 보는 지표. 어제 '반등 ≠ 폭넓은 회복' 기사 단어.

review.q: The 10-year Treasury ______ rose to 5.1%. 빈칸에 알맞은 단어는?
review.exp_ko: yield = (채권) 금리·수익률. 오늘 기사에서도 미 10년 금리는 약 5.1% 수준.

review.q: After the big drop, bargain hunters stepped in. 무슨 뜻?
review.exp_ko: bargain = 싼 물건, hunter = 찾는 사람 → 떨어졌을 때 싸게 사는 저가 매수자. step in = 개입하다/들어오다.

quiz.q: 'The company's guidance was weak.' 에서 guidance의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
quiz.exp_ko: guidance = 회사 스스로 낸 실적 전망. GM은 이익은 좋았지만 이 전망이 기대보다 낮아 7.5% 떨어졌다.
경기가 나빠도 사람들이 꼭 사는 음식·약 관련 회사가 방어주(defensive). 자동차·코인 채굴주는 경기에 민감하다.

quiz.q: According to the text, which index ended Tuesday almost flat?

talk.topic: Tech out, health care in — 돈이 기술주에서 방어주로 이동
talk.setting_ko: 점심시간, 주식하는 회사 동료 둘이 어제 미국장 얘기를 한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see the market last night? Tech basically went nowhere.
dialogue.ko: 어젯밤 장 봤어? 기술주 그냥 제자리더라.

dialogue.en: Yeah, but health care went crazy. It hit a record high.
dialogue.ko: 응, 근데 헬스케어가 난리였어. 사상 최고치 찍었대.

dialogue.en: Looks like a lot of people decided to play it safe.
dialogue.ko: 사람들이 안전하게 가기로 한 것 같네.

dialogue.en: Makes sense. Rates are still around five percent, so nobody wants to chase expensive tech.
dialogue.ko: 그럴 만해. 금리가 아직 5% 근처니까 비싼 기술주를 쫓아가고 싶진 않겠지.

dialogue.en: And GM got crushed, down like seven and a half percent.
Their numbers were fine, though. It was the guidance that scared people.
dialogue.ko: 실적 자체는 괜찮았는데, 가이던스가 사람들을 겁먹게 했지.

dialogue.en: So are you jumping ship from tech?
Nah, I'm just gonna sit tight and ride it out.
dialogue.ko: 아니, 그냥 가만히 버티면서 지나가길 기다릴래.

expressions.ex: My stock went nowhere all week.
I played it safe and kept some cash.

expressions.when_ko: 하던 것을 버리고 다른 쪽으로 옮길 때
expressions.ex: A lot of investors jumped ship from tech to health care.
Just sit tight until the earnings come out.

your_turn.q_en: If the market got scary, would you jump ship or sit tight? Why?
your_turn.hint_ko: I'd probably ~ because ~ 구조로 이유 2개. play it safe / sit tight 써보기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I'd probably sit tight. I mean, I've jumped ship before and it didn't really work out — I sold too early and missed the rebound. So now I try to play it safe from the start, like keeping some cash on the side, and then I don't have to panic.

talk.setting_ko: 주말 오후, 붐비는 동네 카페. 노트북을 들고 들어온 손님(A)과 직원·옆 손님(B).

dialogue.en: Hi, can I get an iced Americano? Large, please.
dialogue.ko: 안녕하세요, 아이스 아메리카노 하나요. 큰 걸로요.

dialogue.en: Sure. For here or to go?
For here. Wow, it's packed in here today.
dialogue.ko: 먹고 갈게요. 와, 오늘 사람 꽉 찼네요.

dialogue.en: Yeah, weekends are always like this. There might be a spot by the window.
dialogue.ko: 네, 주말엔 늘 이래요. 창가 쪽에 자리 있을 거예요.

dialogue.en: (to another customer) Excuse me, is this seat taken?
No, go ahead. The outlet's right under the table, by the way.
dialogue.ko: 아뇨, 앉으세요. 아 그리고 콘센트는 테이블 바로 밑에 있어요.

dialogue.en: Oh, perfect. Mind if I plug in my laptop here?
dialogue.ko: 오, 딱이네요. 여기 노트북 꽂아도 될까요?

dialogue.en: Not at all. I'm leaving soon anyway.

expressions.when_ko: 카페·패스트푸드 주문 때 꼭 듣는 질문
expressions.ex: For here, please. I'm gonna stay a while.
It was packed in there, so we went somewhere else.
Excuse me, is this seat taken?

expressions.when_ko: 공손하게 허락을 구할 때 (대답은 'Not at all' = 괜찮아요)
expressions.ex: Mind if I sit here for a bit?

expressions.when_ko: 말하다가 정보를 덧붙이거나 화제를 바꿀 때
expressions.ex: By the way, the Wi-Fi password is on the receipt.

your_turn.q_en: Tell me about a cafe you like to go to. What do you usually order and what do you do there?
your_turn.hint_ko: 위치 → 분위기 → 주문 메뉴 → 거기서 하는 일(공부·음악 듣기) 순서로 4~5문장.
your_turn.sample_answer: There's this small cafe near my place that I go to almost every weekend. It's pretty cozy, with big windows and kind of chill music. I usually get an iced Americano, even in winter, you know. I just sit by the window, put on my earphones, and read market news or plan my workouts for the week. It's packed on Saturdays, so I try to go early.

combo.q_en: You indicated in the survey that you go to the gym. Tell me about the gym you usually go to. Where is it, and what does it look like inside? Please describe it in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 헬스장에 다닌다고 하셨네요. 평소 다니는 헬스장에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 안은 어떻게 생겼나요? 최대한 자세히 묘사해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(위치·첫인상 한 줄) → 본문 ① 구역별 공간 묘사(입구–유산소–프리웨이트–스쿼트랙) ② 내가 주로 쓰는 기구+근육 이름(quads·hamstrings·lats) ③ 분위기·사람·감정 → 마무리(왜 좋아하는지). 90초~2분, 현재시제 일관. IH/AL 포인트: 공간 순서대로 '걸어가듯' 묘사, 구체적 숫자·위치어(on the left, in the back), 필러 1~2회.
combo.model_answer: Okay, so the gym I go to is just, like, a five-minute walk from my apartment. It's on the second floor of a building right above a convenience store, so it's super easy to get to. When you walk in, there's a front desk on the right, and then the cardio area with maybe ten treadmills facing a big window. Honestly, I don't spend much time there. Most of my time is in the back, in the free-weight section. There are two squat racks, a deadlift platform, and a long row of dumbbells. On leg day, I basically live in the squat rack — squats for my quads and glutes, and then Romanian deadlifts for my hamstrings. On the other side there are cable machines, and I use the lat pulldown a lot for my back. The vibe is pretty chill, actually. It's not too crowded, people are friendly, and the music is loud enough to keep me going. I mean, it's not fancy at all, but it's clean and it has everything I need. That's why I've been going there for years.

key_phrases.en: It's just a five-minute walk from ~
When you walk in, there's ~ on the right.
I basically live in the squat rack.
It's not fancy at all, but it has everything I need.
key_phrases.ko: 전혀 화려하진 않지만 필요한 건 다 있어요

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '기구 나열', IH는 '공간을 걸어가듯 순서대로', AL은 거기에 '내가 그 공간에서 뭘 하는지(근육·루틴)+감정'까지 붙인다.

combo.q_en: How has your workout routine changed since you first started going to the gym? Compare what you did back then with what you do now.
combo.q_ko: 처음 헬스장에 다니기 시작했을 때와 비교해 운동 루틴이 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 그때 했던 것과 지금 하는 것을 비교해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(처음 시작한 시기 한 줄) → 본문 ① 그때(과거시제: used to / would — 아무 계획 없이, 유산소·머신 위주) ② 계기(전환점 한 문장) ③ 지금(현재시제: 분할 루틴, progressive overload, 기록) → 마무리(변화에 대한 느낌·앞으로 계획=미래시제). IH/AL 핵심: 과거↔현재 시제 전환을 정확히, while/compared to로 대조, 자기수정 1회.
combo.model_answer: Oh, it's totally different now. When I first started, maybe like five or six years ago, I had no idea what I was doing. I used to just jump on the treadmill for thirty minutes and then try a few random machines. I'd do, like, bicep curls every single day because I thought that's what working out was. And to be honest, I didn't see much change. Then a friend of mine — actually, he was my coworker at the time — showed me how to do a proper split routine. That was kind of a turning point. These days I train four days a week: push, pull, legs, and then upper body. On leg day I focus on squats for my quads and Romanian deadlifts for my hamstrings. The biggest difference is progressive overload. I write down every set in an app, and I try to add a little weight or one more rep each week. So back then I was just moving around, while now I actually have a plan. Next year, I'm hoping to hit a hundred-kilo squat, so wish me luck.

key_phrases.en: I had no idea what I was doing.
That was kind of a turning point.
Back then I was just ~, while now I actually ~.

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '예전엔 A, 지금은 B' 두 문장으로 끝, IH는 '전환점(계기)'을 넣어 이야기로, AL은 used to/would(과거 습관)→현재→미래 계획까지 시제 3개를 자연스럽게 잇는다.

combo.q_en: Gyms and fitness trends have changed a lot over the years. How are gyms today different from gyms in the past? What kinds of changes have you noticed?
combo.q_ko: 헬스장과 운동 트렌드는 몇 년 사이 많이 바뀌었습니다. 요즘 헬스장은 예전과 어떻게 다른가요? 어떤 변화를 느꼈나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(크게 변했다 + 변화 2가지 예고) → 본문 ① 변화1: 시설·기술(앱, 24시간, 출입) ② 변화2: 사람들(여성·노년층 증가, 근력운동 인기, SNS) ③ 내 생각·감정(장점+작은 단점) → 마무리. 사회 변화형 질문이라 'people these days ~' 일반 주어 사용. AL 포인트: 변화를 '예고→전개' 구조로 정리하고 원인까지 한 줄 덧붙이기.
combo.model_answer: Hmm, let me think. I'd say gyms have changed in two big ways. First, the facilities. Back in the day, gyms were kind of dark and old, and you had to pay for, like, a whole year at the front desk. These days, a lot of gyms are open twenty-four hours, and you just scan a QR code on your phone to get in. Some even have apps that track your workouts. Second, and this is the bigger change, the people are different. In the past, it was mostly young guys trying to get big arms. But now I see all kinds of people — women doing heavy deadlifts, older people doing squats for their knees and hip health. I think social media played a huge role. People post their workouts online, so lifting became, you know, kind of trendy. Personally, I think it's a great change. The only downside is that the squat racks are always taken after work. But overall, it feels more open and more welcoming than it used to be.

key_phrases.en: I'd say ~ have changed in two big ways.
key_phrases.ko: ~는 크게 두 가지가 바뀐 것 같아요

key_phrases.en: Back in the day, ~ / These days, ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '요즘 헬스장 좋아요' 감상, IH는 변화 2개를 예시로, AL은 '두 가지'로 예고하고 First/Second로 정리 + 원인(social media)과 단점까지 균형 있게 말한다.

useful.when_ko: 비교 문제 과거 파트 시작할 때

useful.en: Compared to when I first started, ~

useful.when_ko: 변화가 매우 클 때 감정 강조

useful.en: Let me put it this way, ~
useful.when_ko: 말이 막힐 때 시간 벌면서 다시 설명

opic.practice_ko: 2번(루틴 변화) 문제를 타이머 2분에 맞춰 녹음 → 다시 들으며 과거(used to/I'd)와 현재 시제가 섞였는지 체크. 두 번째 녹음 땐 'It's like night and day'와 근육 이름 2개(quads·hamstrings)를 꼭 넣기.

aptitude.q: 10월 20일(미국) S&P500은 전일 대비 0.22% 상승한 7,707.57로 마감했다. 전일 종가에 가장 가까운 값은?
GM이 제시한 연간 주당순이익 가이던스는 12.75~13.75달러이고, 애널리스트 예상 중간값은 13.41달러다. 가이던스 중간값은 애널리스트 예상보다 약 몇 % 낮은가?
10월 20일 코스피에서 외국인은 5,382억 원, 기관은 10,011억 원을 순매도했고 개인은 9,036억 원을 순매수했다. 개인 순매수는 외국인·기관 순매도 합계의 약 몇 %인가?
aptitude.exp_ko: 외국인+기관 순매도 = 5,382+10,011 = 15,393억. 9,036÷15,393 ≈ 0.587 → 약 59%. 나머지 약 41%는 프로그램·기타 주체 등에서 메워졌다(이 문제에선 계산만).
